questions.enonce_markdown: A car of mass $750\ \mathrm{kg}$ is moving up a straight road inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = \tfrac{1}{15}$. The resistance to the motion of the car from non-gravitational forces has a constant magnitude of $R$ newtons. The power developed by the car's engine is $15\ \mathrm{kW}$ and the car is moving at a constant speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find $R$. (Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Along the slope (positive up the slope) the forces on the car are the driving force $D$ of the engine (up the slope), the resistance $R$ (down the slope) and the component of the weight $mg\sin\theta$ (down the slope). The speed is constant, so the acceleration is zero and $D = R + mg\sin\theta$.

Power $=$ driving force $\times$ speed, so

$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{15\,000}{20} = 750\ \mathrm{N}$$

Component of the weight: $mg\sin\theta = 750\times 10\times\tfrac{1}{15} = 500\ \mathrm{N}$. Hence

$$750 = R + 500 \;\Rightarrow\; R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$$

**$R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: A car of mass $750\ \mathrm{kg}$ is moving up a straight road inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = \tfrac{1}{15}$. The resistance to the motion of the car from non-gravitational forces has a constant magnitude of $R$ newtons. The power developed by the engine of the car is increased to $18\ \mathrm{kW}$ and the non-gravitational resistance remains the same, when the car is moving up a road at a speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find its acceleration. (Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Same road, same $R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$ (from part (a)), positive direction up the slope. At the instant when the speed is $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ the driving force is

$$D' = \frac{18\,000}{20} = 900\ \mathrm{N}$$

Newton's second law along the slope:

$$D' - R - mg\sin\theta = ma \;\Rightarrow\; 900 - 250 - 500 = 750\,a \;\Rightarrow\; a = \frac{150}{750} = 0.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**The acceleration is $0.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$** up the slope.
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: A bead is threaded on a straight wire. The vector equation of the wire is $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k} + t(2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$. The bead is moved from point $A$ on the wire through a distance of $6\ \mathrm{m}$ along the wire to a point $B$ by a force $\mathbf{F} = (7\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$. Find the magnitude of the work done by $\mathbf{F}$ in moving the bead from $A$ to $B$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** The wire is a straight line with direction vector $\mathbf{d} = 2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$, of length $|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3$. The force $\mathbf{F}$ is constant, so the work it does is $W = \mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{s}$, where $\mathbf{s}$ is the displacement from $A$ to $B$.

The unit vector along the wire is $\tfrac13\mathbf{d}$, so a displacement of $6\ \mathrm{m}$ along the wire (in the direction of increasing $t$) is

$$\mathbf{s} = 6\times\tfrac13(2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}) = (4\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$$

$$W = \mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{s} = (7)(4) + (4)(-2) + (-2)(4) = 28 - 8 - 8 = 12\ \mathrm{J}$$

(Check: the component of $\mathbf{F}$ along the wire is $\mathbf{F}\cdot\tfrac13\mathbf{d} = \tfrac{14 - 4 - 4}{3} = 2\ \mathrm{N}$, and $2\ \mathrm{N}\times 6\ \mathrm{m} = 12\ \mathrm{J}$.)

If the bead were moved the other way along the wire, $\mathbf{s}$ would be reversed and the work would be $-12\ \mathrm{J}$; the magnitude is the same.

**The magnitude of the work done by $\mathbf{F}$ is $12\ \mathrm{J}$.**
